title: The complete workspace
caption: Everything lives in one HTML file: the parts library on the left, the schematic canvas in the middle, the panel stack on the right, the waveform analyzer along the bottom, and the toolbar across the top. No install, no server, no accounts.

title: Preset picker
caption: Twenty-one boards ship with the tool, from a ripple counter to a PC/XT that boots FreeDOS. Loading one replaces the board, the program and the waveform selection.

title: Start / Stop
caption: Start runs the design checks, programs the ROMs, proves the memory map by probing your netlist, and builds the simulation.

title: Pause / Resume
caption: Freezes simulated time. Pausing also leaves turbo, because stepping and probing want full fidelity.

title: Step one cycle
caption: One clock half-step. This is how you watch a bus cycle assemble itself: address out with ALE, strobe low, data sampled, strobe high.

title: Step one instruction
caption: Runs exactly one instruction, however many bus cycles that takes.

title: Speed
caption: Ten stops from two steps per second up to max: 2, 10, 60, 300, 1500, 8000, 40k, 200k, 1M, then uncapped.

title: Turbo
caption: Compiles the board's clock tree and batches CPU execution to reach real 8088 speed. Waveform capture pauses while it is engaged.

title: Rewind
caption: Scrubs backwards through recorded history — the whole machine returns to how it was, not a replay.

title: Undo / redo
caption: Every board edit is one step. An accepted autowiring plan — however many wires and created chips it involved — is also one step.

title: Guided lab
caption: Appears for the nine boards that ship an exercise: numbered steps you tick off as you work.

title: No-wire mode
caption: Hides every wire while leaving the netlist intact. Click a chip and only its connections are drawn.

title: Complete the board
caption: Scans the whole board, offers every hookup that is possible right now, and repairs connections that have gone missing.

title: Themes
caption: Twenty colour schemes, ten dark and ten light.

title: Status
caption: Simulated time, cycles, instructions retired, and the measured clock rate.

title: The parts library
caption: Every modelled chip and device, grouped by category. Click a part, then click the canvas to place it. The library locks while the simulation runs.

caption: Each lane names its signal and shows the value at the cursor, or now: 0, 1, Z or X for pins, hex for buses.

title: Lane height 60%
caption: Vertical zoom runs from 60% to 250%; the signal names resize in lockstep so labels stay aligned to their lanes.

title: Lane height 160%
caption: Vertical zoom runs from 60% to 250%; the signal names resize in lockstep so labels stay aligned to their lanes.

title: Lane height 250%
caption: Vertical zoom runs from 60% to 250%; the signal names resize in lockstep so labels stay aligned to their lanes.

title: The time cursor
caption: Click anywhere to drop a cursor: it reports the half-step and the cycle number, and every lane reports its value at that moment.

title: The history scrollbar
caption: The recording keeps up to 131,072 half-steps. Drag the bar to browse it; drag to the right edge to re-attach to live time.

title: Add any signal
caption: Every chip on the board, expandable to its pins, with automatic bus groups (⛁ A0..A19) that become a single hex lane.

title: An interrupt on the wire
caption: On the interrupt lab the default signal set includes INTR and ~INTA — watch INTR rise, then two ~INTA pulses, the second carrying the vector on AD0-7.

title: The unified memory view
caption: One hex editor across the whole address space, writing through the proved map.

title: Where everything answers
caption: The range dropdown lists every window the prober found, marking aliases — the mirrors partial decoding creates — and the reset vector.

title: Chip-local hex editor
caption: Double-click a memory chip for its own bytes, always addressed from zero — the chip's point of view, with no knowledge of where the board maps it.

title: The ROM, byte by byte
caption: The assembled program as it sits in the EPROM — including the far jump at the reset vector that starts the machine. Hand edits here are kept when you press Start; pressing Assemble reclaims the ROM for the code pane.

title: Memory while running
caption: The view is live: watch the stack change as CALLs push, or find the byte your program just wrote.

title: A full PC memory map
caption: On the XT board the same prober finds 512K of RAM, the video window, the option ROM and the BIOS — each measured, not declared.

title: The disk image library
caption: Built-in FreeDOS media plus your own images, kept in the browser between sessions: insert, attach, duplicate, export, import, or populate from a folder on your machine.

title: Creating media
caption: Format blank 360K, 720K or 1.44M floppies, or a 10.4 MB hard disk — all FAT12, all written by the tool's own filesystem code.

title: The floppy drive
caption: Motor and IRQ lamps, the diskette in the bay with its geometry, a running count of sectors read and written, and buttons to insert, eject, format or write the image back to your machine.

title: Browsing a real FAT12 disk
caption: The FreeDOS diskette, read by the tool's own FAT12 implementation: browse directories, download files out, copy files in, or format fresh media.

title: The PC/XT board
caption: CPU, DMA, interrupt controller, timer, PPI, floppy controller, XT-IDE, serial port, Hercules card, keyboard and speaker — a complete machine on one canvas.

title: D1 — SPKR
caption: The speaker shows its cone moving and labels the frequency it is being driven at.

title: D2 — SW8
caption: The configuration switches — flip them while the machine runs and the BIOS sees a different machine next boot.

title: D3 — UPD765
caption: The floppy controller, moving sectors over DMA channel 2.

title: D7 — XTKBD
caption: A full XT-84 keyboard drawn key by key — press a key on your own keyboard and you can see it depress here.

title: D8 — HGC
caption: The Hercules card: 32K of video RAM, a 6845-style CRTC, and real HSYNC/VSYNC/VIDEO outputs.

title: D9 — CRT
caption: The monitor renders live from the video card's frame buffer, right on the schematic.

title: The CRT window
caption: A full phosphor screen rendered from the real Hercules frame buffer — with scanlines, glow and glare — and the on-screen XT keyboard docked beneath it.

title: The keyboard dock
caption: Click the keys, or type on your own keyboard: either way real scancodes travel the serial line into the shift register and raise IRQ1.

title: Video from a bare 8088
caption: No BIOS, no operating system: an 8088 writing characters straight into video memory at B000:0000.

title: Seven-segment display
caption: Common cathode, driven from a '373 output port, with the digits decoded in software from a segment table.

title: LEDs on a PPI port
caption: An 8255 drives a traffic light from port A — the whole board was wired by autoconnect.

title: The printer
caption: A Centronics printer with a real BUSY/ACK handshake — and paper you can read.

title: The speaker
caption: The 8253 in mode 3 is a square-wave synthesiser; the symbol shows the live frequency.

title: DIP switches
caption: Eight switches you can flip while the machine runs.

title: The serial terminal
caption: Green phosphor on the other end of the wire: the 8250's transmit stream, and a box to type back down the line.
